answer: A useful sybil defense is to require each agent to lock scarce, slashable stake before it can submit work, then randomly assign tasks and pay only after independent agents verify the result. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply influence: each must tie up real capital, and dishonest submissions risk losing it. The island can host the registry, while zephyr routes tasks and the kernel checks attestations; none of those names makes an identity costly without the stake rule.
